;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War]]
**A local politician is [[kidnapping|abducted]] and killed by [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] militants in [[Balad, Somalia|Bal'ad]], [[Middle Shabelle]], [[Somalia]]. [https://www.voanews.com/africa/al-shabab-militants-abduct-kill-somali-lawmaker (Voice of America)]
*[[American-led intervention in Iraq (2014–2021)]]
**A [[Katyusha rocket launcher|Katyusha rocket]] falls in the [[Green Zone]] of [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]], injuring a child and damaging a house. [[Iraqi security forces]] also thwart another rocket launched at [[Camp Taji]], which houses [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. troops]]. Also, a [[MIM-104 Patriot]] defense system shoots down a missile launched against the [[Embassy of the United States, Baghdad|U.S. embassy]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/07/05/Rocket-attack-on-Baghdad-Green-Zone-injures-child-damages-house.html (Al Arabiya)]
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]]
**The [[Government of National Accord]] (GNA) warns of a "response in the right place and at the right time" after a "foreign air force" bombed the [[Al-Watiya Air Base]] in an overnight air raid, according to the GNA's Deputy Defence Minister Salah al-Namrush. Al-Namrush did not specify which foreign air force was behind the raid, which is believed to have targeted a [[Turkish Armed Forces|Turkish]] [[anti-aircraft warfare|anti-aircraft]] missile system. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/libya-gov-vows-response-base-hit-foreign-air-force-200705183314172.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Hachalu Hundessa riots]]
**The death toll amid civil unrest in [[Oromia Region]], [[Ethiopia]], rises to 166 people, including 11 security personnel. More than 1,000 people have been arrested. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-53298845 (BBC News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
**The [[government of India|government]] extends the lockdown in the city of [[Agra]] and delays the reopening of the [[Taj Mahal]] for tourists and visitors after a spike in COVID-19 cases in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-india-monuments/india-puts-back-taj-mahal-reopening-citing-covid-19-risks-idUSKBN24606U?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Mercedes-Benz]] announces that it will be recalling 668,954 vehicles in [[China]] over possible issues with oil leakage. [https://apnews.com/e3a4ea5994a938564bb67084e23854ef (AP)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Kyushu floods]]
**The death toll from floods in [[Kumamoto Prefecture]], [[Japan]], rises to 20 and 14 people remain missing. [[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Shinzo Abe]] meets with a disaster task force team to step up rescue efforts. Meanwhile, weather agencies warn people to remain alert as more rains are predicted. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-japan-floods/flood-death-toll-hits-20-as-japan-warned-of-more-rainfall-idUSKBN24604A (Reuters)]
*Eight people are feared dead following a [[mid-air collision]] between two planes flying over [[Lake Coeur d'Alene]] in [[Idaho]], US, both of which then crashed into the waters. Two of the victims' bodies have already been recovered. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/05/us/idaho-plane-collision-coeur-dalene-lake/index.html (CNN)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
****[[Michigan]] reports no new deaths from COVID-19 for the first time since March 17. [https://www.mlive.com/news/2020/07/michigan-reports-no-new-coronavirus-deaths-for-first-time-since-march.html (MLive.com)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
***[[Iran]]'s [[Ministry of Health and Medical Education]] reports the highest daily death toll to date from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], recording 163 deaths. Iran's cases reach 240,438 while the deaths jump to 11,571. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-iran/iran-records-highest-daily-death-toll-from-covid-19-idUSKBN2460FL?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[List of mass shootings in the United States in 2020]]
**At least two people are killed and eight injured, four critically, in a [[mass shooting]] at a nightclub in [[Greenville, South Carolina]]. No suspects have been arrested. [https://www.wyff4.com/article/at-least-12-injured-in-shooting-at-upstate-bar-deputies-say/33192716 (WYFF)] [https://apnews.com/faf507c074e0df2ae1f24f54fb12c49f (AP)] [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/05/us/greenville-south-carolina-shooting/index.html (CNN)]
**In [[Atlanta]], a large group of people were watching fireworks when a gunfight broke out after a car hit a pedestrian. Fourteen people were wounded, of which two were declared dead at the hospital. [https://www.wsbtv.com/news/local/atlanta/19-people-shot-two-different-atlanta-shootings-police-say/NXQLSNPZVJDXHN3IRMFT6UWFAQ/ (WSB-TV)] 
**The incidents were part of a violent [[Independence Day (United States)|Independence Day]] weekend across in the United States which left 160 people dead and over 500 more wounded in shootings. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/jul/07/gun-violence-shootings-fourth-of-july-weekend-racism-segregation (''The Guardian'')]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Arizona]], [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**An [[Arizona]] woman in [[Scottsdale, Arizona|Scottsdale]] is arrested at [[Target Corporation|Target]] after pulling face masks off the displays. [https://popculture.com/trending/news/watch-qanon-karen-arrested-raging-against-target-face-mask-display-rolex/ (popculture.com)] [https://www.nydailynews.com/coronavirus/ny-coronavirus-woman-trash-face-mask-display-target-store-arizona-20200706-uckcggzegjexfgu5ozq4yhjmuu-story.html (''New York Daily News'')]
*A bus driver in the French city of [[Bayonne]] is left [[Brain death|brain dead]] after reportedly being assaulted by passengers who refused to wear face masks. Bus services in the city have been severely disrupted as drivers refuse to work following the incident. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53309424 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Dominican Republic general election]]
**After having been postponed once due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Dominican Republic|COVID-19 pandemic]], [[Elections in the Dominican Republic|general elections]] are held in the [[Dominican Republic]]. The electorate can vote for the new members of the [[Senate of the Dominican Republic|Senate]] and [[Chamber of Deputies of the Dominican Republic|Chamber of Deputies]] as well as the country's next [[President of the Dominican Republic|president]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-53268860 (BBC News)]
**Conservative candidate and opposition leader [[Luis Abinader]] is proclaimed the winner, ending 16 years of centre-left rule. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-53268860 (BBC News)]
*[[2020 Croatian parliamentary election]]
**[[Croatia]] holds [[Elections in Croatia|parliamentary elections]] amid the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia|COVID-19 pandemic]]. Rising infection rates and the pandemic's effects on the economy might influence the outcome of the election. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-croatia-election/croatia-holds-election-amid-sharp-economic-downturn-rising-coronavirus-infections-idUKKBN246005 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 New Caledonian independence referendum]]
**The [[Labour Party (New Caledonia)]] expresses its support for independence from [[France]] in the upcoming [[referendum]], the party leader [[Louis Kotra Uregei]] says after abstaining in 2018. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/420568/new-caledonia-labour-party-wants-independence (RNZ)]
*[[Yuriko Koike]] wins her second term as [[Governor of Tokyo]]. [https://apnews.com/8b4e8bb3c246c1af04335b9d3e5d2825 (AP)]
